text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. To get good results, users often practice prompt engineering—writing clear instructions to guide the model. LLMs can answer questions, translate languages, and help with writing. However, they also have limits. They may produce wrong information, cannot truly understand meaning, and depend heavily on the quality of their training data.
